newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria, Sierra Leone sign military training pact.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria, Sierra Leone sign military training pact.

text.p: Nigeria and Sierra Leone have signed a military training cooperation agreement, a Nigerian defence headquarters spokesman said on Saturday.
Colonel Godwin Ugbo told Reuters the Status of Forces Agreement (SOFA) was signed on Friday for Nigeria to extend its military and police training in Sierra Leone.
"We have been training their forces since 1994 under an agreement that expired last year and this new SOFA is to renew and expand the old one," he said.
Chief of defence staff Major-General Abdulsalam Abubakar signed for Nigeria while Sierra Leone's deputy defence minister retired Captain Sam Norman signed for his country.

"We recognise our size which is small. We recognise the size of Nigeria, which is bigger," Norman was quoted by The Guardian newspaper as saying at the signing ceremony. "We have a responsibility to protect our people," he added.

Nigeria, the regional power in West Africa, has a battalion of troops in Sierra Leone, who helped to protect installations in the capital Freetown during that country's five-year civil war with rebels of the Revolutionary United Front (RUF).
